dog.definition: A domesticated animal commonly kept as a companion.
dog.exampleUsage: The dog waits beside its owner.

cat.definition: A small domesticated animal commonly kept as a companion.
cat.exampleUsage: The cat rests in its carrier.

rabbit.definition: An animal with long ears, strong back legs and a short tail.

hamster.definition: A small rodent with cheek pouches, sometimes kept as a pet.
hamster.exampleUsage: The hamster carries food in its cheek pouches.

parrot.definition: A bird with a curved beak, often with brightly coloured feathers.
parrot.exampleUsage: The parrot sits on a perch.

turtle.definition: A reptile with a protective shell around its body.
turtle.exampleUsage: The turtle waits in a secure transport container.

guinea-pig.definition: A small domesticated rodent often kept as a pet.
guinea-pig.exampleUsage: The guinea pig waited in a secure carrier.

fish.definition: An animal that lives in water, usually with fins and gills.
fish.exampleUsage: The fish swims in the tank.

snake.exampleUsage: The snake rests in a secure enclosure.

ferret.definition: A small domesticated mammal with a long body, related to the polecat.
ferret.exampleUsage: The ferret waits in a secure carrier.

stethoscope.definition: An instrument used to listen to sounds inside the body.
stethoscope.exampleUsage: The veterinarian places the stethoscope on the clean table.

thermometer.definition: An instrument used to measure temperature.
thermometer.exampleUsage: The veterinary technician prepares the thermometer.

scale.definition: A device used to measure an animal’s weight.
scale.exampleUsage: The vet checks the dog’s weight on the scale.

otoscope.definition: An instrument with a light used to examine the ear.
otoscope.exampleUsage: The veterinarian prepares the otoscope for the examination.

x-ray.definition: A medical image made using X-rays to show structures inside the body.
x-ray.exampleUsage: The veterinarian examines the dog’s X-ray.

ultrasound.definition: A medical imaging method using high-frequency sound waves.
ultrasound.exampleUsage: The veterinarian explains the ultrasound examination.

blood-test.definition: A laboratory examination of a blood sample.
blood-test.exampleUsage: The vet discusses the blood test results with the owner.

microscope.definition: An instrument that makes tiny objects look larger.
microscope.exampleUsage: The lab technician examines the sample with a microscope.

syringe.definition: A tube with a plunger used by trained staff to draw up or deliver liquid.
syringe.exampleUsage: The veterinary technician prepares a syringe.

bandage.definition: A strip or piece of material used to cover or support an injured body part.
bandage.exampleUsage: The veterinarian checks the animal’s bandage.

vaccination.definition: Giving a vaccine to help protect against a disease.
vaccination.exampleUsage: The owner asks about the pet’s vaccination appointment.

surgery.definition: A medical operation performed by a trained veterinary professional.
surgery.exampleUsage: The veterinarian discusses surgery with the pet owner.

dental-cleaning.definition: A professional cleaning procedure that removes plaque and tartar from an animal's teeth, usually performed by veterinary staff.
dental-cleaning.exampleUsage: The veterinarian discussed whether the pet needed dental cleaning.

microchip.definition: A tiny electronic identification device placed under an animal’s skin by a veterinary professional.
microchip.exampleUsage: The clinic scans the dog’s microchip to read its identification number.

spay.definition: To perform an operation that prevents a female animal from reproducing.
spay.exampleUsage: The owner asks the veterinarian when to spay the cat.

neuter.definition: To perform an operation that prevents an animal from reproducing, often used specifically for males.
neuter.exampleUsage: The owner asks the veterinarian about the decision to neuter the dog.

medication.definition: Medicine used under appropriate professional guidance.
medication.exampleUsage: The owner asks how to follow the prescribed medication instructions.

stitches.definition: Threads or other materials used by a medical professional to close a wound or surgical cut.
stitches.exampleUsage: The veterinarian checked that the stitches were healing normally.

cast.definition: A firm covering used by a veterinary professional to support a broken or injured body part.
cast.exampleUsage: The veterinarian checks the cast on the dog’s leg.

cone-collar.definition: A cone-shaped protective collar worn by an animal to stop it licking or biting a wound.
cone-collar.exampleUsage: The dog wore a cone collar after treatment.

waiting-room.definition: A room where clients and animals wait before being seen by veterinary staff.
waiting-room.exampleUsage: The cat stayed in its carrier in the waiting room.

exam-table.definition: A raised table used to support an animal during a veterinary examination.
exam-table.exampleUsage: The vet gently examined the puppy on the exam table.

operating-room.definition: A specially equipped room where qualified staff perform surgery.
operating-room.exampleUsage: The operating room is separate from reception.

kennel.definition: A shelter or enclosure for a dog.
kennel.exampleUsage: The dog rests in its kennel.

pharmacy.definition: The area where medicines are stored and dispensed by qualified staff.
pharmacy.exampleUsage: The owner collects the prescribed medicine from the clinic pharmacy.

reception.definition: The area where visitors arrive, check in and ask for information.
reception.exampleUsage: The receptionist welcomes the owner at reception.

lab.definition: A room where staff examine samples and perform scientific tests.
lab.exampleUsage: Staff take the sample to the lab.

recovery-room.definition: A room where animals are monitored after an operation or treatment.
recovery-room.exampleUsage: Staff monitor the animal in the recovery room.

grooming-area.definition: A designated space for washing, brushing, trimming, or other pet-grooming tasks.
grooming-area.exampleUsage: The clinic has a separate grooming area.

outdoor-run.definition: A secure outdoor enclosure where an animal can move around for exercise.
outdoor-run.exampleUsage: The boarding area includes a secure outdoor run.

leash.definition: A strap or cord attached to an animal to keep it close during a walk.
leash.exampleUsage: Omar keeps the dog on a leash.

carrier.definition: A secure portable container used to transport an animal.
carrier.exampleUsage: The cat stays in its carrier in the waiting room.

muzzle.definition: A covering over an animal’s mouth used when professionally appropriate to reduce biting risk.
muzzle.exampleUsage: The owner asks the vet whether the dog needs a muzzle.

treats.definition: Small portions of food offered as rewards or occasional extras for an animal.
treats.exampleUsage: The owner checks whether these treats are suitable for the dog.

food-bowl.definition: A bowl used to hold an animal’s food.
food-bowl.exampleUsage: The owner washes the food bowl after the meal.

water-dish.definition: A shallow container used to provide drinking water for an animal.
water-dish.exampleUsage: The water dish is beside the enclosure.

collar.definition: A band worn around an animal’s neck.
collar.exampleUsage: The dog has a plain collar.

tag.definition: A small label attached to a collar to identify the animal.
tag.exampleUsage: The owner checks the tag on the collar.

nail-clippers.definition: A small tool designed to trim an animal’s claws.
nail-clippers.exampleUsage: The groomer puts the nail clippers beside the brush.

brush.definition: A tool with bristles used to clean or smooth an animal’s coat.
brush.exampleUsage: The groomer puts the brush on the table.

veterinarian.definition: A professional qualified to diagnose and treat animals.

vet-tech.definition: A trained veterinary technician who assists veterinarians with animal care and clinical tasks.
vet-tech.exampleUsage: The vet tech prepared the examination room.

receptionist.definition: A worker who welcomes visitors, answers calls and manages appointments.
receptionist.exampleUsage: The receptionist checks the appointment time.

groomer.definition: A person who cleans and cares for an animal’s coat.
groomer.exampleUsage: The groomer prepares the brush and towel.

kennel-attendant.definition: A worker who feeds, cleans, monitors, and cares for animals kept in kennels.
kennel-attendant.exampleUsage: The kennel attendant refreshed the animals' water.

surgeon.definition: A veterinary professional who performs operations on animals.
surgeon.exampleUsage: The surgeon speaks with the pet owner before the operation.

specialist.definition: A veterinary professional with expertise in a particular area of animal medicine.
specialist.exampleUsage: The vet refers the animal to a specialist.

intern.definition: A qualified veterinary graduate gaining supervised practical experience.
intern.exampleUsage: The intern works under the veterinarian’s supervision.

volunteer.definition: A person who freely helps without being paid.
volunteer.exampleUsage: The volunteer helps staff organise the waiting room.

pet-owner.definition: A person who owns and is responsible for a companion animal.
pet-owner.exampleUsage: The pet owner described the cat's recent behavior to the vet.
